subject: Post-call: Crestline Labs inference discovery — mutual action plan & topology
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha@crestlinelabs.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@crestlinelabs.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Sep 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Crestline Labs inference discovery — mutual action plan & topology

Hi Aisha / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. Please flag anything I misunderstood.

Summary of what you shared
- Primary product: Crestline Assist (document understanding + retrieval-augmented generation).
- Pain: 95/99p latency spikes when queries hit long context windows; user-facing SLA target is 300ms P95 for single-turn responses.
- Throughput: production traffic forecast ~80–120 QPS peak, with strong diurnal spikes (burst to ~200 QPS for short windows).
- Cost: current provider costs are eating into margins; team needs path to 30–40% reduction in per-request inference cost.
- Quality: some degradation with aggressive quantization — must preserve top-1 answer fidelity for safety-critical intents.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 Type II evidence required; must support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for keys.

Initial technical posture we discussed
- Recommended PoC topology: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool in us-west) + autoscale for burst.
- Model strategy: run a high-quality 13B chat model quantized to int8/4 for cost, with an unquantized fallback at lower concurrency for highest-fidelity requests.
- Latency approach: continuous batching with smart latency SLO routing — small requests routed to low-latency pool, long-context/expensive requests failover to a spot of higher-memory nodes.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (we estimate 15–25% token savings within your workflow).

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP) — immediate next steps
1) Crestline: share a 500–1,000-sample anonymized prompt set + example response scoring rubric (by Sep 9).
2) Redwood: provide a PoC topology sketch, expected cost estimate for 3 traffic profiles, and a 4-week PoC plan (by Sep 6).
3) Crestline procurement: share procurement timeline & any required contract addendum for SOC2/VPC (by Sep 16).
4) Technical deep-dive: schedule a 90min infra session with your platform team to nail network/KMS details (propose Sep 7 or Sep 8).

Attachments: I’ve attached a short requirements worksheet and a draft mutual action plan for signatures.

Questions/unknowns we called out
- Can Crestline share anonymized latency traces for a 24-hour window? That will let us size KV cache and pod counts more accurately.
- Do you expect synchronous single-turn only, or multi-turn chat (session affinity / KV cache lifetime implications)?

If that looks right I’ll: 1) book the deep-dive (tentatively Sep 7 @ 10am PT), 2) hand to Priyom/Karthik to draft the topology and cost sketch, and 3) open the MAP in HubSpot.

Thanks — Jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: Crestline Labs inference discovery — mutual action plan & topology

On Sat, Sep 2, 2028 at 3:12 PM Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com> wrote:
> (summary omitted)

Thanks Jasmine — good recap. Adding a few technical clarifications from our end so Crestline has visibility into the PoC assumptions.

Technical notes
- Topology sketch (high level): 3x low-latency pods (A100/RTX-class) pinned to small-seq workloads + 2x high-memory pods for long-context batching and fallback. Autoscale policy to add up to +3 burst pods when queue depth > 40 requests.
- KV cache: expect 10–20% hit rate for typical RAG flows with 24–48h TTL; if you can provide sampled traces we can refine.
- Model variants: recommend starting with a 13B chat variant in int8, validated against your rubric. If fidelity regression > 3% on your scoring, we keep an fp16 model for the critical intents (cost/latency trade off documented).
- Quantization profile: int8 with selective full-precision for attention layers; avoids worst-case hallucination patterns we’ve seen in bulk int4 configs.
- Telemetry: need a short-lived API key to push PoC telemetry (latency, token counts, KV hit rates) into a staging project. We only use it for sizing and will delete after PoC.

Deliverables from Redwood for PoC (target Sep 6)
- Topology diagram (GDrive link), cost estimate for low/medium/high traffic, SLO mapping doc (P95/P99 budgets), configuration for caching and routing.

Aisha — let me know if the topology approach aligns with your infra constraints (esp. VPC peering). Happy to walk this through on the deep-dive.

— Priyom

--
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0198

Date: Sun, 03 Sep 2028 09:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Crestline Labs inference discovery — mutual action plan & topology

Thanks Jasmine & Priyom — that all matches my notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

What we can provide
- We can produce a 500-sample anonymized prompt set by Sep 9 (derived from low-sensitivity logs).
- We will share a short scoring rubric for safety-critical intents (we care about top-1 fidelity).
- Procurement: target window is late Sep; budget is constrained so we’ll need a clear cost delta vs current provider.

Constraints / asks
- SOC 2 Type II evidence is required before we can move to production; please include your SOC2 scope and approximate delivery timeline in the PoC packet.
- We need a clear fallback plan if an int8 variant deviates from the rubric; please document automatic rollback conditions.
- Network: VPC peering is preferred; if not possible we can consider a private endpoint and strict IP allowlist.

Ok to proceed with the Sep 7 10am PT deep-dive. Tom will coordinate with our infra to join.

Thanks — Aisha

Aisha Patel
Head of Product, Crestline Labs
aisha@crestlinelabs.com | +1 212-555-0107

Internal note (not sent to Crestline):

Thanks team — good momentum. Quick action assignment before the deep-dive: 
- Priyom: topology diagram + cost scenarios (low/med/high) + SLO mapping. Target: Sep 6 EOD. (Deliver to Drive, link in MAP).
- Karthik: prep a short runbook for model fallback & automatic rollback thresholds (include rollback latency triggers and fidelity regression thresholds). Target: Sep 6 EOD.
- Jasmine: book the deep-dive (confirmed Sep 7 @ 10am PT), update HubSpot MAP, and attach the requirements worksheet.

We should avoid promising SOC2 delivery dates until security confirms the scope; I’ll loop in Security if Crestline pushes SOC2 acceptance as a gating item.

Jasmine
